brief: A tool rack that hangs on a wall from keyhole hangers, with hooks for small hand tools.

requirements.requirement: Tool rack that hangs on a wall from keyhole hangers
requirements.evidence: Two hex-acc-keyhole accessories (accessory:1#-1,0#1 and accessory:1#1,0#1) on the rear faces of the left and right ends of the upper storey of a 3-wide x 2-tall rack (6 full cells), so the rack lifts onto and drops over wall screws at two points.

Six hex-acc-hook plates (two hooks each, 12 hooks total): three on the front faces of the lower storey and three on the front faces of the upper storey (accessory:0#...#4 and accessory:1#...#4), one per cell. Two cable coils hang on the upper-left and upper-right hooks (prop:1, prop:2) showing the hooks in use.

requirements.requirement: Rack holds together as one wall-mounted unit
requirements.evidence: capOpenFaces capped 8 open faces and lockJoints added joint bolts on the upper storey (jointBolt:1#-1,0#0, jointBolt:1#0,0#0); check_build reports no issues and meshClash clear. The configurator checks fit only, so wall-screw load capacity is not verified.

finish.summary: A 3-wide, 2-tall Hex Cluster rack (6 full cells, 43 parts with caps and joint bolts). Two keyhole hangers on the rear of the top storey's end cells let it drop onto wall screws; six hook plates (12 hooks) across both front rows take small hand tools, with two cable coils hung on the upper hooks to show them in use. Note a gaffer-tape roll would not hang on the centre upper hook (it overlaps the neighbouring cell wall per the configurator), so that hook is left empty. check_build is clean with meshClash clear.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
